 Getting a Real ID in NJ Now Won’t Get You Through TSA by Thanksgiving
 Devin Marchetti 
 Published Nov 15, 2026 
 Thanksgiving is 11 days away, and anyone in New Jersey still flying on an old license has a timing problem. A Real ID booked now will most likely arrive in the mail after the holiday, and the paper copy you get at the MVC does not work at airport security.
 Do You Need a Real ID to Fly in New Jersey?
 Yes, for domestic flights, unless you have another ID that TSA accepts. Standard licenses stopped working at airport checkpoints on May 7, 2025 .
 A New Jersey Real ID has a star in the upper right corner. A standard license says “NOT FOR REAL ID PURPOSES” instead, and TSA will not take it.
 Atlantic City International is the closest airport for much of South Jersey. (Brian, CC BY-SA 2.0) 
 You do not need a Real ID if you can bring one of these, according to TSA’s list .
 A U.S. passport or passport card
 A Global Entry, NEXUS, SENTRI or FAST card
 A military ID, including for dependents
 A green card or a work permit card
 A Veteran Health Identification Card
 TSA still accepts these up to two years after they expire. Travelers under 18 do not need any ID for flights inside the U.S.
 The paper license from the MVC does not work at TSA, and the card takes about two weeks to arrive. 
 Can You Get a Real ID in NJ Before Thanksgiving?
 You can get one, but you probably cannot fly on it by Thanksgiving. The MVC gives you a temporary paper license at your appointment and mails the real card within about two weeks , the governor’s office says . Some people have waited longer.
 TSA’s rules say plainly that a temporary license is not an acceptable ID. So someone who books this weekend and goes in midweek would get the card around the start of December, after the Sunday rush home on Nov. 29.
 Booking now still makes sense for Christmas trips. Appointments are easy to get right now, with an average wait of about three days , down from 73 days in January, the state says.
 What Happens at TSA Without a Real ID?
 You can pay $45 for TSA ConfirmID, which checks who you are another way. The fee covers 10 days of travel, so one payment works for a Thanksgiving round trip.
 Pay online at tsa.gov/confirmid before you leave, by card, bank account, PayPal or Venmo. Airports do not take cash for it. Bring the receipt and whatever ID you have.
 Expect it to take 10 to 15 minutes at the checkpoint, and possibly 30 minutes or more. TSA also warns it cannot promise it will be able to confirm your identity, and if it cannot, you will not get through.
 That matters this year. Sunday, Nov. 29 is expected to be one of the busiest days TSA has ever had, and Philadelphia International already tells domestic travelers to arrive two hours early.
 Philadelphia International tells domestic travelers to arrive two hours early. (Dough4872, CC BY-SA 4.0) 
 How Do You Get a Real ID in NJ?
 Book an appointment at REALID.nj.gov . Your first Real ID has to be done in person, and the MVC does not take walk-ins for it.
 First Real IDs are done in person at an MVC licensing center. (Tomwsulcer, CC0) 
 If your license runs out within three months, book a renewal appointment and upgrade at the same visit. If not, book a Real ID appointment and keep your current expiration date.
 Bring originals or certified copies of these.
 Two proofs of your NJ address , such as a utility bill, bank statement or pay stub. These can now be shown on your phone.
 Your Social Security number . Bring the card, a W-2 or a pay stub showing the full number in case the MVC cannot confirm it.
 ID documents worth 6 points , starting with a passport or a certified birth certificate. The MVC’s document selector tells you exactly what counts.
 Real ID points are not the same as the regular 6 Points of ID for a standard license, so check the selector before you go.
 How Much Does a Real ID Cost in NJ?
 $35 for a four-year Real ID, or $11 to upgrade early and keep your current expiration date. A standard license is $24.
 For a real emergency trip within 30 days, the MVC runs an expedited program for people with no passport or other accepted ID. It costs $80 extra, takes at least three business days and is only done by appointment at the Trenton Regional Center.
 Where Can You Get a Real ID in South Jersey?
 Every MVC licensing center in South Jersey handles Real ID appointments. Cherry Hill is a vehicle center only and does not.
